findings.title: `canManage()` grants group management permission to callers with only `view` scope on all-groups
findings.body: In `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()`, line 70 calls `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. Because `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` checks `auth.groups().requireManage()`, any caller who is granted only the `view` scope on the all-groups resource (`Groups`) will pass `canManage()` and be able to create or move top-level groups in the realm. `canManage()` should only check `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` (and the Javadoc on `GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage()` at line 75 should be updated accordingly).

findings.title: `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` passes authz resource ID instead of group ID and returns resource IDs
findings.body: When `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` creates a group resource, it sets the resource's `name` to `group.getId()` (while `resource.getId()` is the newly generated UUID of the authorization `Resource`, and for the all-groups resource `name` is `"Groups"`). In `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, lines 121-125 iterate over resources of type `Groups` and: (1) pass `groupResource.getId()` to `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)`, which looks up `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` — because `findByName` matches the group ID (stored in `resource.getName()`), looking up by `groupResource.getId()` returns `null` and falls back to the all-groups resource instead of evaluating the specific group resource; and (2) add `groupResource.getId()` (the authz resource UUID) to `granted` instead of `groupResource.getName()` (the actual group ID), causing user queries filtered by `UserModel.GROUPS` to match no users (unless the all-groups resource itself is matched, which also has name `"Groups"` rather than a group ID).

findings.title: `canCreateGroupMembers` checks only V1 feature flag, breaking user creation via group permissions in V2
findings.body: `UsersResource.canCreateGroupMembers` (line 178) returns `false` when `!Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)`. When `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is enabled (and V1 is disabled), an admin with `manage-members` and `manage-membership` permissions on a group cannot create a user directly in that group via `POST /users`, because `canCreateGroupMembers` immediately returns `false` instead of evaluating the group permissions.

findings.title: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName` does not handle `GROUPS` resource type
findings.body: In `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName` (lines 328-350), only `USERS.getType().equals(resourceType)` is handled to resolve the human-readable resource name, while `GROUPS` (and `CLIENTS`) fall through to `resource.getDisplayName()`. Because `getOrCreateResource` creates group resources with `name = group.getId()` and no display name, policies/permissions for groups will return `null` (or raw UUIDs) as the resource name in representations instead of `"All groups"` or the group's name/path.

findings.title: Javadoc on `requireManageMembers` references `canManageMembership` instead of `canManageMembers`
findings.body: On line 133 of `GroupPermissionEvaluator.java`, the Javadoc for `requireManageMembers(GroupModel group)` states `Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canManageMembership(GroupModel)} returns {@code false}`, but the method actually checks `canManageMembers(GroupModel)`.
